status: prospective development-then-confirmation protocol; NOT preregistered: the repairs were chosen from the findings of the earlier studies
question: do the recommended repairs (metric-consistent weighting, converged solver, full-simplex L2 fit, scale-aware penalty, extended lambda grid + 1-SE rule, CV-anchored scales, post-fit merge) make AKDE more accurate and/or more compact, and does the repaired estimator still fall behind the conventional comparators?

development.fold_stream: method index 0 for every variant (shared folds, as Stage A)
development.purpose: ablation and finalist selection only; never reported as confirmation

selection_rule.primary: equal-weight-per-cell geometric mean, over the 8 Marron-Wand dev cells, of the paired ISE ratio variant / I0_finalist (lower is better)
gates: geometric-mean ratio vs I0 on the 4 hr dev cells <= 1.0
stage-1 AND stage-2 KKT at tolerance in >= 90% of dev fits (stage-1 n/a for simplex_l2)
no execution error; all fits valid densities
selection_rule.tie_break: among variants whose primary ratio is within 10% of the best, prefer the one with fewer tuned hyperparameters, then lower mean wall time
selection_rule.ablation_to_confirm: the finalist; plus I4_simplex_l2 if the finalist is not I4 (the parameter-free core), so the contribution of anchor/merge is confirmed too

confirmation.fold_stream: method index 6 (finalist) and 7 (ablation): Stage-C policy, datasets identical to Stage C so comparisons with the saved Stage-C rows of AKDE-M, AKDE-V2, SPADES-simplex, KDE-SJ, Abramson, GMM-EM are paired on data

metrics: query latency on saved models (10000 identical points, batch 2000, 2 warmup, 7 repeats, median within model)
large-error flag: ISE > 5x own cell median

analysis.benchmark: equal-weight-per-target mean ISE; fixed-benchmark exp(T) paired ratio vs AKDE-M and vs SPADES-simplex / KDE-SJ / Abramson / GMM
analysis.tables: mean +- SD; bootstrap intervals only in labelled tables/figures

solver_tolerances.simplex_l2: fully corrective Frank-Wolfe, 400 rounds, active-set subproblems
